title: Continuous rational realization of the raw constructible derived category
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$, where localization is the sheaf colimit of repeated multiplication by $\varpi$. The sheaves $B_X$ and $E_X$ are canonically the continuous coefficient sheaves $U\mapsto C(|U|,A)$ and $U\mapsto C(|U|,E)$, respectively, with the finite-quotient constant-section normalizations. Use sheaves of modules and their ambient derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. An $E_X$-module sheaf is called constructible if on every member $S$ of some finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification] its restriction is pro-etale locally a finite free $E_S$-module, with finite rank allowed to vary. Let $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E_X)$ be the full ambient derived subcategory of bounded complexes with such cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

The functor on integral representatives
$$J_X(QK)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K,\qquad J_X(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}J_X(f),$$
from the raw localization $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] of the completed integral category with compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], is an $E$-linear equivalence of triangulated categories onto $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E_X)$. It identifies the bounded localized t-structure [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] with the ambient standard t-structure restricted to this subcategory, and its heart with the constructible $E_X$-module sheaves in degree zero. In particular $J_X(\mathcal H^r(QK))$ is the ordinary sheaf $E_X\otimes_{B_X}\mathcal H^r(K)$ in degree zero.

For a morphism $g:X'\to X$ between schemes satisfying these hypotheses, the completed pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], extended to raw rationalizations, is carried by $J$ to ordinary derived module inverse image
$$\mathbb Lg^*_{E}(C)=E_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}C.$$
This comparison is natural and compatible with identity and composition of scheme morphisms and with finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset L$ and its associators. The composition comparisons here are those of these ambient derived module inverse images. For an etale morphism or locally closed immersion, $g^{-1}E_X\cong E_{X'}$ canonically and the module inverse image is the exact ordinary inverse image. For a pro-etale site object $U\to X$, restriction sends $E_X$ to $E_U$ and is the exact site-restriction functor; these identifications apply also to the restriction of the displayed ambient pullback. All coefficient comparisons are induced by the finite quotient maps, localization and the balanced tensor maps.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), with Lemma 6.8.2(1), Proposition 6.8.11(3), Definition 6.8.8 and Remark 6.8.15; completed-ring presentation via Proposition 6.6.11. Scalar-extension and composition compatibility refer to the canonical coefficient and tensor comparisons.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,A)$ for the completed-coefficient category, including its compatible etale-origin witnesses. The coefficient datum defines $B_X=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X$ as a ring sheaf with its specified projections. The continuous-coefficient restriction lemma identifies this ring with $V\mapsto C(|V|,A)$, and identifies its sheafified localization at $\varpi$ with $V\mapsto C(|V|,E)$. The identifications preserve constant sections and quotient projections and commute with locally closed restriction. All categories below are categories of module sheaves over these actual ring sheaves.

The integral stratified-perfect characterization applies to $X$: it assumes exactly a finite coefficient field, a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme, and invertibility of $\ell$. It says that $K\in\mathcal C_X$ if and only if $K$ is bounded and its cohomology, on a finite stratification, is locally $B_S\otimes_A N$ for finitely presented $A$-modules $N$. Equivalently its local models are $B_S\otimes_A^L P$ with $P$ perfect. In particular it puts such integral sheaves in degree zero in $\mathcal C_X$, and supplies closure under shifts, cones, truncations and cohomology. This step concerns the integral category only; it does not yet identify its rationalization with the target category.

Scalar localization of module sheaves is exact by the localization/inverse-image coherence lemma, applied to the identity geometric morphism with $R=B_X,t=\varpi$. Its termwise derived functor is $F_X(K)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$, as also given by derived change of rings. Exactness implies $\mathcal H^r(F_XK)=E_X\otimes_{B_X}\mathcal H^r(K)$: an exact functor preserves the kernels, images and quotients defining cohomology. On a stratum $h:S\to X$ the continuous-coefficient restriction lemma gives $h^{-1}B_X\cong B_S$ and $h^{-1}E_X\cong E_S$, and the coherence lemma (for $h$) commutes $h^{-1}$ with localization; so on an integral local model this sheaf is $E_S\otimes_A N$. A finitely presented module over the DVR $A$ has a finite presentation; after tensoring the presentation with the field $E$, its cokernel is a finite-dimensional vector space, so the last sheaf is locally finite free. Thus $F_XK$ lies in $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E_X)$. Since $\varpi$ acts invertibly after $F_X$, the fraction relation defines $J_X(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$, respecting addition, identities and composition. Raw scalar localization is triangulated with distinguished triangles isomorphic to integral image triangles; hence the triangulated functor $F_X$ induces a triangulated $E$-linear functor $J_X$ into the ambient $D(\operatorname{Mod}(E_X))$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2): construction of the functor; Lemma 6.8.2

proof.text:
For $K,L\in\mathcal C_X$, verify the Hom-continuity hypothesis of the scalar-localization Hom lemma. Integral bounded-below compactness gives the global-derived-Hom coproduct comparison for every countable family with a common lower bound, including its shift by any integer $q$. Take $H^0$ and use the global-sections/internal-Hom comparison to identify $H^0R\operatorname{Hom}(K,M)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B_X)}(K,M)$. Countable sums of $A$-modules are exact, since finite-support coordinates preserve kernels and surjections; their termwise sums represent derived sums by the countable-sums lemma. Thus $H^0$ of their sum is the sum of their $H^0$'s. These observations give precisely the Hom/coproduct hypothesis, and boundedness makes $L$ bounded below. The scalar-localization Hom lemma, with $R=B_X,t=\varpi$, now gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B_X)}(K,L[q])[1/\varpi]\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(E_X)}(F_XK,F_XL[q]),\quad f/\varpi^n\longmapsto\varpi^{-n}F_X(f).$$
At $q=0$ the left side is the raw category's Hom group. The lemma's identity and composition clauses prove full faithfulness of $J_X$. The target here is $D(E_X)$, not $D(B_X)$.

Apply the directed-triangulated-image lemma with the singleton preorder, source the raw rationalized category, identity transition, and functor $J_X$ to the ambient $D(E_X)$. Step 3 gives a triangulated functor and Step 4 gives every arrow between its image objects an actual lift; these are the lemma's hypotheses at the unique common stage. Its conclusion makes the essential image closed under zero, shifts and distinguished triangles. If $L$ is a lisse $E_X$-sheaf, the lisse-lattice lemma produces a constructible $B_X$-module $N$ with $E_X\otimes_{B_X}N\cong L$. Step 2 puts $N[0]$ in $\mathcal C_X$, with completeness and compatible etale origins. Hence all lisse sheaves in degree zero belong to the essential image.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13; Proposition 6.8.14(2), lattice and cone argument

proof.text: Let $F$ be a constructible $E_X$-module sheaf. To use the finite-model stratum-filtration tool, take the condensed ring $C(-,E)$. The continuous-coefficient realization identifies its pulled ring on every scheme with the continuous ring sheaf, naturally for coefficient maps. The internal/sectionwise module equivalence preserves underlying sheaves and actions. Thus a finite free model $E_S^r$ is exactly the tool's finite constant local model $E_S\otimes_E E^r$. This identification is used only for the sheaf filtration, never to infer membership in the completed integral category. Choose the finite noetherian affine cover of $X$. The affine-noetherian-space lemma makes each member noetherian. A descending closed chain stabilizes on each of these finitely many members, hence stabilizes globally. Thus $|X|$ is noetherian, and the filtration lemma applies and gives a finite filtration of $F$ with quotients $v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$, where $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$ is qcqs open and $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ is reduced closed. Each local model of $L_k$ is a finitely presented $E$-module, hence a finite-dimensional vector space; therefore $L_k$ is lisse.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), finite stratification devissage; filtration tool uses Stacks Tag 09Y5

proof.text: Each $S_k$ is noetherian, finite-dimensional and $\ell$-coprime: it is closed in the noetherian open $V_k$, affine rings are quotients of noetherian rings, irreducible closed chains have the dimension bound from $X$, and the inverse of $\ell$ survives in the quotient local rings. Choose a constructible integral lattice $N_k$ for $L_k$ by the lisse-lattice lemma. The ringed open-closed lemma supplies exact $v_{k!}$ and $(t_k)_*$, and their restrictions are $N_k$ on the supporting pieces and zero on the complements. Extending the finite stratification of $N_k$ by those zero pieces proves $M_k=v_{k!}(t_k)_*N_k$ is an integral constructible sheaf; Step 2 certifies $M_k[0]\in\mathcal C_X$, including the etale witnesses. Locally closed coefficient restrictions are the maps of Step 1. Localization is the sequential sheaf colimit of multiplication by $\varpi$, with fractions as transition classes. It commutes with $v_{k!}$ since that functor is a left adjoint, and with $(t_k)_*$ by the filtered-colimit clause of the open-closed lemma on the qcqs $V_k$. Module colimits are the underlying abelian sheaf colimits. Therefore $J_X(QM_k)\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), integral models for the filtration quotients; Lemma 6.8.13

proof.text: Induct over the finite filtration of Step 6, beginning with its zero term. Its short exact sequence $0\to F_{k-1}\to F_k\to v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k\to0$ is a distinguished triangle in $D(E_X)$ by the short-exact-sequence clause of the heart-triangle lemma for the ambient standard t-structure. Step 7 and the induction hypothesis put its outer terms in the essential image. The connecting morphism lifts by full faithfulness, and the cone closure in Step 5 puts $F_k$ in the image. This proves that every constructible $E_X$-sheaf in degree zero has an integral derived model; it does not assert a globally lisse integral lattice.

For $C\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E_X)$ choose a finite cohomological interval $[a,b]$ and induct on its length. An object with zero cohomology is zero in the derived category. Otherwise its standard truncation triangle has terms $\tau^{\leq b-1}C,C,\mathcal H^b(C)[-b]$. The first has a shorter interval and the third lies in the image by Step 8 and shift closure. Step 5 gives extension closure, or equivalently lifts the connecting arrow and takes its cone. Thus $C$ is in the image. Together with Steps 3 and 4 this proves the asserted $E$-linear triangulated equivalence. In particular the full target subcategory inherits the ambient distinguished triangles; no idempotent envelope is introduced.

The integral t-structure proposition identifies integral truncations and cohomology with the ambient ones and keeps them in $\mathcal C_X$. The localized t-structure proposition gives $\tau_E^{\leq m}QK\cong Q\tau_A^{\leq m}K$ and the analogous upper formula. Exact scalar localization gives the cohomology formula of Step 3, so $J_X$ sends the two localized degree-bound classes into the corresponding ambient degree-bound classes. In particular it is t-exact in this direction, and $J_X(\mathcal H^r(QK))$ is $E_X\otimes_{B_X}\mathcal H^r(K)$ placed in degree zero.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3) and 6.8.14(2): cohomology and forward degree bounds

proof.text: Conversely, if $J_X(QK)$ has no cohomology above $m$, then Step 3 and the integral truncation formula show $J_X(Q\tau_A^{\geq m+1}K)$ has zero cohomology in every degree. It is zero in the derived category, so full faithfulness implies $Q\tau_A^{\geq m+1}K=0$ (its identity is zero). The localized truncation triangle then gives $Q\tau_A^{\leq m}K\cong QK$, putting $QK$ in the localized nonpositive class at $m$. The same argument with $\tau_A^{\leq m-1}K$ proves the converse nonnegative bound. Hence both t-structures agree under $J_X$. Uniqueness of truncation triangles, with their canonical units and counits, makes the truncation comparisons natural. Intersecting the two degree bounds identifies the heart with all constructible $E_X$-sheaves in degree zero, using Step 8 for their essential surjectivity.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2): converse degree bounds and truncation/heart identification

proof.text: Fix $g:X'\to X$ as in the statement. Use the actual structural map $c_g:g^{-1}B_X\to B_{X'}$ defined by its finite quotient components, not an assumed isomorphism. Pull back a supporting stratification of $K\in\mathcal C_X$; its base changes form a stratification of $X'$. The trivializing pro-etale covers pull back to covers by weakly etale base change and fpqc covering stability. On each pulled-back cover, ordinary derived module pullback sends $B_S\otimes_A^L P$ to $B_{S'}\otimes_A^L P$: on the finite projective terms the balancing map is $b'\otimes(b\otimes p)\mapsto b'c_g(b)\otimes p$, with inverse $b'\otimes p\mapsto b'\otimes(1\otimes p)$. These maps commute with differentials. Derived pullback is computed on K-flat flat-term resolutions; its tensor and composition comparisons identify this local computation with the restriction of $Lg^*_{B}K$. Every new stratum is locally closed in the noetherian finite-dimensional $X'$, so has the same scheme hypotheses. The stratified-perfect characterization therefore gives $Lg^*_{B}K\in\mathcal C_{X'}$, including derived completeness and compatible etale-origin witnesses.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Remark 6.8.15: ordinary pullback preserves the integral category

proof.text:
The specified comparison $\gamma_{g,K}:Lg^*_{B}K\to Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ is the quotient-tower completion unit by the completed-pullback definition and the constant/completed comparison. Step 12 makes its source complete. Intrinsic completeness says its Koszul completion unit is invertible, and the constant-completion equivalence identifies that unit with this quotient-tower unit, including transitions. Thus $\gamma_{g,K}$ is invertible, naturally in $K$. Apply localization/inverse-image coherence to $R=B_X,t=\varpi$. It identifies $g^{-1}E_X$ with $(g^{-1}B_X)[1/\varpi]$, preserving the localization unit. The map $c_g$ sends $\varpi$ to $\varpi$, so it extends to the structural map into $E_{X'}$. The ringed-topos derived pullback composition comparison now gives
$$J_{X'}(Q Lg^*_{B}K)\cong E_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}(E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K).$$
Both sides flatten to $E_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}B_X}g^{-1}K$ by balancing. Composing this comparison with $J_{X'}(Q\gamma_{g,K}^{-1})$ proves the displayed completed-pullback comparison. Its naturality and the fraction rule let it descend to raw rationalizations.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; Stacks Tag 099M (completion units) and Tag 099N as specified by the completed-pullback node

proof.text: For composable scheme maps $X''\xrightarrow h X'\xrightarrow g X$, the structural maps satisfy $c_{gh}=c_h\,h^{-1}c_g$ after the inverse-image composition comparison: composing with each finite quotient projection gives the same finite constant-coefficient map, and the limit universal property gives equality. The ambient derived pullback composition and identity comparisons are those of the ringed-derived monoidal-comparison lemma. Localization/inverse-image coherence identifies the comparison for $gh$ with the composite comparisons for $g,h$, as an equation of natural transformations. On K-flat complexes the tensor maps send a balanced representative $e''\otimes e'\otimes k$ to $e''h^{-1}(e')\otimes k$ in either order; the identity sends $1\otimes k$ to $k$. These maps give the comparisons in Step 13. Under the natural completion units $\gamma$, completed pullback on this category is ordinary pullback; conjugating by those isomorphisms gives exactly the same equations. The finite-reduction and completion-unit comparisons used here preserve the quotient maps, so the conjugation uses the specified units, not arbitrary identifications. This proves naturality, identity and composition with the ambient composition comparisons stated in the item.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15: specified ambient identity and composition comparisons

proof.text:
For a finite extension $E\subset L$, put $A_L=\mathcal O_L$ and $B_{L,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_L/\varpi_L^n)_X$. The raw scalar-extension proposition defines $T_{L/E}$ by the actual integral change $C_{L/E,X}K=B_{L,X}\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$ followed by rationalization, and puts this object in the integral category under our scheme hypotheses. Continuous-coefficient realization is natural for $A_E\to A_L$ and $E\to L$, so these are the stated continuous ring maps. Apply the ambient derived pullback composition comparison to the same-site coefficient maps. It gives
$$J_{L,X}(T_{L/E}QK)=L_X\otimes^L_{B_{L,X}}(B_{L,X}\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K)\cong L_X\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K\cong L_X\otimes^L_{E_X}J_{E,X}(QK).$$
The maps flatten $(l\otimes b)\otimes k$ to $lb\otimes k$, with inverses inserting $1$. They are canonical on K-flat representatives, and the comparison lemma descends them to derived categories. The image of every nonzero scalar of $E$ is invertible in $L$, so the equations also hold for the raw morphisms $f/\varpi_E^n$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2); coefficient naturality of Lemma 6.8.2 and ordinary derived tensor balancing

proof.text: For $E\subset L\subset M$ both routes in the coefficient associator comparison flatten $m\otimes l\otimes k$ to $ml\otimes k$. For four fields the pentagon flattens all factors to their ordered product; the unit inserts and removes $1$. The ringed-derived comparison lemma makes these equations valid on derived complexes; the raw scalar-extension proposition identifies these associators with its specified ones. To combine with $g:X'\to X$, the square of the integral structural maps $c_g$ and coefficient change commutes, since on each quotient the two composites are postcomposition of the same coefficient map and inverse image of the same section. The continuous realization's coefficient naturality gives the localized square as well. The last clause of the ringed-derived comparison lemma for isomorphic underlying geometric composites identifies the two derived tensor routes. Its balanced map sends $l'\otimes b'\otimes k$ to $l'b'\otimes g^{-1}k$ in either order. The completion-unit comparisons of Step 13 and the scalar-extension/pullback comparison in the raw scalar-extension proposition preserve this equation. Thus the realization comparison commutes with finite coefficient extension, successive extensions, and their pullback and composition associators. No pair-category descent is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15: finite-field-extension and pullback coherence

proof.text: For a locally closed immersion the coefficient isomorphism is precisely the continuous-coefficient immersion restriction lemma. For an etale map $g:X'\to X$, use the weakly etale localization equivalence $X'_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq X_{\mathrm{proet}}/X'$. The inverse image $g^{-1}$ of the pro-etale inverse-image definition is this slice restriction: for $U\to X'$ in $X'_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with structure map $s$, the pair $(U\to X,(s,\mathrm{id}_U))$ is initial in the indexing category $\mathcal I_U$, since any $(V,\phi)$ has $\phi=(s,a)$ with $a=\mathrm{pr}_2\phi$ the unique $X$-morphism satisfying $u_g(a)(s,\mathrm{id})=\phi$; hence $(u_{g,p}F)(U)=F(U\to X)$, already a sheaf on the slice, and no sheafification changes it. Restriction to this slice evaluates a coefficient sheaf on the same underlying scheme $V$, so sends $C(|V|,A)$ and $C(|V|,E)$ identically to the corresponding coefficient sheaves on $X'$. In the finite-quotient description it restricts each constant quotient to the same quotient and preserves the sectionwise limit, so the resulting coefficient map is exactly $c_g$, with the constant-section normalizations. The same evaluation argument works for any site object $U\to X$, without requiring $U$ itself to be noetherian. Inverse image with an identified coefficient ring is exact by localization/inverse-image coherence; its termwise derived functor is ordinary inverse image. Hence for the etale and locally closed morphisms the displayed module pullback is exact inverse image, and on an arbitrary site object it restricts to exact site restriction. All identifications preserve coefficient maps by their section formulas and Step 1.
